IndependentFigureConcepts.Title: Cone volume and inverse radius
IndependentFigureConcepts.IndependentMathematicalModel: For a cone with h=2r, use V=2πr³/3 to obtain r=∛(3V/(2π)). Require V≥0 and r≥0.
IndependentFigureConcepts.StudentTeacherExplanation: An inverse of a cubic measurement model returns a physical length from volume.

IndependentFigureConcepts.Title: Physical parabolic trough cross section
IndependentFigureConcepts.IndependentMathematicalModel: Use a symmetric parabolic trough model y=x²/2 and compare widths at nonnegative depths; width w=2√(2y).
IndependentFigureConcepts.StudentTeacherExplanation: Physical dimensions select a nonnegative root even when the mathematical parabola has both signs.

IndependentFigureConcepts.Title: Parabola coordinate restriction
IndependentFigureConcepts.IndependentMathematicalModel: For y=x²/2, restrict x≥0 to obtain x=√(2y), or x≤0 to obtain x=−√(2y).
IndependentFigureConcepts.StudentTeacherExplanation: A full parabola is not one-to-one; each monotone half yields an inverse.

IndependentFigureConcepts.Title: Cubic curve and inverse reflected about y=x
IndependentFigureConcepts.IndependentMathematicalModel: For f(x)=x³+1, f⁻¹(x)=∛(x−1); swap ordered pairs (0,1) and (1,0).
IndependentFigureConcepts.StudentTeacherExplanation: Inverse graphs reflect across y=x; every original input-output pair is swapped.

IndependentFigureConcepts.Title: Both quadratic branches represent different inverse functions
IndependentFigureConcepts.IndependentMathematicalModel: For f(x)=(x−4)², x≥4 gives inverse 4+√x while x≤4 gives inverse 4−√x.
IndependentFigureConcepts.StudentTeacherExplanation: Choosing an inverse branch is dictated by the original restricted domain.

IndependentFigureConcepts.Title: Quadratic and inverse branch reflection
IndependentFigureConcepts.IndependentMathematicalModel: For f(x)=(x−2)²−1, x≥2, inverse g(x)=2+√(x+1), x≥−1.
IndependentFigureConcepts.StudentTeacherExplanation: Graph original and inverse to display reflection and exchange of domain and range.

IndependentFigureConcepts.Title: Quadratic translated vertex and inverse
IndependentFigureConcepts.IndependentMathematicalModel: For f(x)=(x+1)²−3 on x≥−1, inverse −1+√(x+3) for x≥−3.
IndependentFigureConcepts.StudentTeacherExplanation: The vertex coordinate (−1,−3) reverses to (−3,−1) on inverse.

IndependentFigureConcepts.Title: Radical function and inverse reflection
IndependentFigureConcepts.IndependentMathematicalModel: For f(x)=1+√(x−1), x≥1, inverse g(x)=(x−1)²+1 for x≥1.
IndependentFigureConcepts.StudentTeacherExplanation: A square-root curve and its restricted quadratic inverse reflect about y=x.

IndependentFigureConcepts.Title: Radical of a rational function requires nonnegative radicand
IndependentFigureConcepts.IndependentMathematicalModel: For y=√((x−2)/(x+3)), use sign intervals about −3 (excluded) and 2 (included); domain (−∞,−3)∪[2,∞).
IndependentFigureConcepts.StudentTeacherExplanation: A sign chart, not cancellation or taking real square roots of negative values, determines allowable inputs.
